patch.title: 1996 Camry Power Window Moves Slowly, Grinds, or Stops — Owner Report
patch.description: A 1996 Camry owner discussion documents power-window operation that became unreliable. Slow movement, grinding, intermittent operation, or glass that stops does not identify one failed part: the switch, wiring, glass run, regulator, motor, attachment, or power and ground can produce similar symptoms. This is an owner-reported troubleshooting topic, not evidence that every 1996 Camry has a regulator or motor defect.
patch.solution: Secure loose glass before it can fall, then test switch command, power, ground, and voltage drop under load. Inspect the exact door's glass attachment, run channels, regulator, motor, and door-jamb wiring. Replace only the measured failure with a VIN-, production-date-, and door-position-specific part.
symptoms: Window moves slowly or stops
Grinding or clicking inside one door
Glass drops or will not stay raised
Window responds intermittently to the switch

patch.title: Rear Crossmember Corrosion on Salt-Exposed Camrys — Owner Reports
patch.description: Owner discussions document serious rear-crossmember corrosion on individual older Camrys exposed to road salt. They support inspecting an aged vehicle; they do not establish a fleet-wide defect, a shared inside-out mechanism, or a guaranteed progression. Material loss around suspension attachment points is a vehicle-specific structural safety finding regardless of cause.
patch.solution: Have the complete rear crossmember, suspension pickup points, fasteners, and adjacent body structure inspected on a lift. If there is perforation, cracking, looseness, deformation, or attachment-point material loss, do not drive until a qualified structural or suspension professional determines whether the vehicle is safe and repairable. Surface coating is not a repair for missing section thickness; verify any replacement structure by VIN and inspect used parts before installation.
symptoms: Visible scaling or perforation on the rear crossmember
Corrosion near rear suspension attachment points
Rear clunk or alignment change accompanied by structural corrosion

citations.title: ToyotaNation: Camry Rear-Crossmember Corrosion Discussion
ToyotaNation: Rear K-Frame Support Corrosion Discussion

communityRecommendations.content: Do not drive with perforation, cracking, looseness, or material loss at a suspension attachment until a qualified inspection establishes that the vehicle is safe.

patch.title: Rear Suspension Clunk or Loose Feel Over Bumps — Owner Report
patch.description: An owner repair discussion documents rear clunking and a loose or fishtailing feel during multi-component troubleshooting. That outcome does not prove one common failed strut mount, bushing, link, arm, or damper across all cars. Similar sounds can come from cargo or spare-tire hardware, exhaust contact, brakes, a hub, spring seating, fasteners, or suspension wear.
patch.solution: Remove or secure cargo and spare-tire hardware, reproduce the noise under controlled conditions, and inspect fastener torque, witness marks, exhaust clearance, brakes, hubs, springs and seats, dampers, mounts, stabilizer links and bushings, and suspension-arm bushings with the suspension appropriately loaded. Replace only a measured loose, torn, leaking, worn, or damaged component; align the vehicle when the repair changes geometry.
symptoms: Rear clunk or knock over bumps
Loose-feeling rear response
Rattle from the rear on rough pavement

patch.title: Oil Leak at the Drain Plug After Service — Owner Reports
patch.description: Owner discussions document drain-plug leaks or damaged threads after oil service on individual Camrys. This is a service-related condition, not evidence of a sixteen-year model defect. A leak at the plug can involve a missing or reused gasket, plug damage, dirt, sealing-face damage, incorrect torque, cross-threading, cracked or deformed pan material, or oil traveling from above.
patch.solution: Confirm the leak source, then inspect the plug, gasket, sealing face, pan material, and threads. Choose repair only after measuring the damage and checking wall thickness, alignment, and chip-control requirements. Do not install an oversize or self-tapping plug or insert from this page without a qualified assessment and the exact service procedure.
symptoms: Fresh oil at the drain plug after service
Drain plug will not tighten normally
Damaged or missing drain-plug gasket
Visible thread or sealing-face damage

patch.title: Rough or High Idle, Stalling, or Pedal-to-Start Concern — Owner Reports
patch.description: Owner and how-to discussions describe throttle-body cleaning during troubleshooting of idle or starting concerns. They do not establish faster-than-normal deposit buildup or prove that deposits cause every rough or high idle, stall, hesitation, or pedal-to-start event. Battery voltage and relearn state, air leaks, PCV flow, MAF data, fuel delivery, ignition, compression, temperature inputs, throttle actuation, and ECM logic can produce overlapping symptoms.
patch.solution: Record stored codes and scan data, check battery and charging voltage, inspect the complete induction system for leaks, and follow Toyota's exact engine diagnostic procedure. Inspect the throttle bore only when the symptom and data support it. If cleaning is selected, use the applicable service instructions and do not force an electronic throttle plate or spray solvent into electronics.
symptoms: Rough or unstable idle
Unexpectedly high idle
Stalling or difficult starting
Hesitation with no confirmed cause

patch.title: 2018 Camry Shift Shock or Delayed Reacceleration — Toyota T-SB-0330-17
patch.description: Toyota T-SB-0330-17 covers some 2018 Camrys with the A25A-FKS engine and UA80E transaxle that exhibit a shift shock on initial startup or a delay followed by a shock when reaccelerating after slowing to about 5-10 mph. Applicability is limited by production change and VIN; the bulletin does not support a 2019-2023 defect claim or every hesitation, harsh shift, or gear-hunting complaint.
patch.solution: Confirm the exact engine, transaxle, production VIN, symptom, and current calibration against Toyota T-SB-0330-17. A qualifying vehicle follows the bulletin's Health Check and Engine/ECT ECU reprogramming procedure with battery support and warranty-label documentation. Other symptoms, DTCs, leaks, or nonqualifying VINs require normal diagnosis rather than assuming this calibration applies.
symptoms: Shift shock on initial startup
Delay followed by a shock when reaccelerating after slowing to about 5-10 mph

patch.title: 2025 Camry ECB or Smart Stop Warnings and Unexpected Driver-Assist Behavior — Owner Reports
patch.description: Complaint indexes contain individual 2025 Camry Hybrid reports involving brake-system messages or unexpected driver-assistance behavior. An ECB or Smart Stop malfunction message, unexpected braking, normal Proactive Driving Assist deceleration, road-sign recognition behavior, and lane-support behavior are different events and must not be assigned one cause. patch.solution: Preserve the exact warning text, timestamp, speed, weather, road markings, driver-assistance settings, and operating conditions. Stop using an assistance function that behaves unexpectedly and arrange prompt Toyota diagnosis. If normal brake response is reduced, stop driving and arrange transport. Check the VIN for open recalls and use stored brake and chassis data; do not assume that sensitivity changes, a feature toggle, or an unspecified software update is a repair.

Driver-assistance behavior that differs from the owner's manual description
Reduced normal brake response
